source_snapshot.items: Test connections between BMC I2C-11, temperature sensor and BMC FRU
source_snapshot.procedure: On BMC run `i2cdetect -y -q 10` then forced `i2ctransfer -f -y 10 w1@0x48 0x00 r2`; consult PID1114953.
source_snapshot.criteria: Only generic evidence/photo and unexpected-log checks; no temperature conversion/range and no FRU endpoint or content oracle.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; invents probing/soldering and ignores the explicit remote sensor read.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY/CHANGED; flags thermal/force-access risk but still invents physical acceptance and incorrectly suggests the0x48 reply can cover FRU mapping without a separate FRU read.
source_snapshot.items_direct_xlsx: Test connections between BMC I2C-11, temperature sensor and BMC FRU
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: "【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). Log into the BMC and run the following command and ensure you get a reply. Refer to PID : 1114953 for other devices expected on the bus. i2cdetect -y -q 10 i2ctransfer -f -y 10 w1@0x48 0x00 r2
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: NO | -- not runnable by agent: testing the physical I2C connection/link between the named components (BMC I2C-11, temperature sensor and BMC FRU) is a hardware-integrity check that requires probing/soldering the actual I2C traces and collecting photos per the criteria; the agent cannot touch the hardware or take photos over SSH.

test_case.test_name: Test connections between BMC I2C-11, temperature sensor and BMC FRU — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify BMC I2C-11 reaches both the temperature sensor and BMC FRU, returning a plausible sensor value and valid immutable FRU identity without disturbing thermal monitoring or EEPROM data.
required_package: PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-11 to Linux bus10, sensor0x48 and BMC FRU endpoint
Temperature-sensor part/revision and register0x00 format, endian, signedness, resolution and valid bits
Expected operating range and correlation tolerance to BMC hwmon/Redfish or independent reference
FRU address, safe header/identity offset/length and format/checksum oracle
Kernel hwmon/FRU driver ownership and approved supported interface or `-f` exception
test_case.test_command: Prove BMC I2C-11 maps to bus10; identify sensor0x48 and the separate FRU EEPROM endpoint; inspect driver ownership; read sensor temperature via supported interface or approved raw register0x00; decode signed/scaled two-byte value and correlate with BMC telemetry/reference; read only approved FRU header/identity bytes and validate signature/checksum; verify no alarms, thresholds or FRU content changed.
test_case.expected_result: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."

Define driver ownership and whether `-f` is allowed, safe scan policy, timeout/NACK/thermal-abort criteria and recovery; confirm physical probing is not mandatory unless separately scoped.
safety_gate: Do not run broad quick-write discovery on bus10
Prefer hwmon/driver reads; do not force0x48 while bound absent explicit approval
Confirm register0x00 read cannot clear alerts or change threshold/pointer state
Read FRU only at approved offsets/length; never write or dump arbitrary protected content
Abort on implausible temperature, alarm/monitoring loss, checksum failure, NACK, timeout, stuck bus or BMC degradation
expected_evidence: PID topology for BMC I2C-11/bus10/sensor0x48/BMC FRU
Sensor/FRU part and firmware/data-format identity plus driver bindings
Vendor temperature register decoder and expected range/tolerance
Timestamped raw two bytes, decoded temperature and simultaneous independent telemetry comparison
Bounded FRU header/identity bytes with expected fields/checksum and no write
Pre/post thermal alarms, FRU integrity, bus/BMC health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Wistron I2C policy requires BMC controller/bus and each target address/expected response. Thermal driver ownership and immutable FRU read boundaries are mandatory.

source_conflict.reason: The source names both sensor and FRU but supplies only an un-decoded0x48 sensor read, no FRU address/content check and no expected temperature. Earlier reviews also impose physical probing absent from the Procedure.
